reviews.text: There's a bit of a wait, but it's a wonderful hospital.

The overwhelming impression is that you're kept waiting.
Even after contacting them via LINE to make a reservation and arriving as instructed, I was kept waiting, and when I thought I was called upstairs, I wasn't called for my examination. In fact, people who arrived after me were being called in one after another, while I was being pushed to the back. I hadn't even requested a specific doctor.

When I checked the waiting times, there were doctors who hadn't received any requests, so I don't understand why I wasn't being called.

Also, I don't know if it's polite or what, but the medication is only given in small batches, so I don't think it's suitable for busy people.

[Cat] Good facilities and appearance, but questionable diagnostic ability and overall treatment plan...

This is a relatively large, well-equipped, and clean hospital in the neighborhood. It might be fine for health checkups and minor symptoms, but for slightly more complex symptoms or cases requiring high diagnostic ability, I was dissatisfied and absolutely cannot recommend it ❌

The first problem occurred during a routine checkup for my elderly cat, who had been taking medication for several years. The veterinarian instructed me to put her on a diet because she was slightly overweight. However, this medication is very sensitive to food intake and weight, and minor changes can be dangerous. At the time, I didn't know the risks and followed the instructions, but I later realized that they hadn't looked at the illness or the medication as a whole, and had only considered weight as a single number.

The deciding factor for switching hospitals was when my cat started vomiting daily and lost her appetite. Blood tests and ultrasound showed abnormal values, but the cause couldn't be identified. I was given anti-nausea medication and told, "Let's see how she does and do more tests next week." There was no concrete answer regarding my cat's loss of appetite, and I felt deeply uneasy about being left untreated without a plan or hypothesis for diagnosis.

Unable to simply wait while watching my beloved cat lose weight day by day, I took her to another hospital in Daikanyama, and the response was completely different. They performed tests with a clear purpose, and it was quickly determined to be a hormonal problem. I'm so glad I switched hospitals, because I don't think what would have happened if we had continued with the same tests. 😮‍💨

While the doctors were polite and professional, I felt compelled to give a critical evaluation because it concerns the health and life of my precious cat.

During my beloved cat's illness, I visited this clinic out of desperation, but it turned out to be an extremely painful experience.

The head veterinarian's attitude was consistently condescending, and he showed no empathy for my anxieties or questions.

What hurt me most was the careless and negligent treatment of my beloved cat, a cherished member of my family.

Furthermore, regarding my cat's condition, the head veterinarian used the phrase "her internal organs were a mess." I was shocked by this expression, which showed no consideration or respect whatsoever for a medical professional. Is such a statement acceptable from a head veterinarian?

This is not a hospital that prioritizes animal lives. It gives the impression that they only value pet owners (customers) with high payment capacity.

Because I lost my cat shortly after the examination, I still feel deep sadness and have many questions regarding the head veterinarian's actions.

Personally, this is not a hospital where I would feel comfortable entrusting my precious family member.

I try to think that it was just his time, but I still can't accept it.
I cry every day. I wish we hadn't had the surgery.
I felt that all the staff members were sincere and reliable, and I could entrust my needs to them with confidence.

I believe this is ideal medical care.
I am a human doctor, but I think everything done at this hospital is appropriate. The informed consent process is thorough, the preparation leading up to surgery, the surgical strategy, and the pathology examinations are all done quickly. They provide incredibly high-level medical care as a matter of course. While I haven't seen many doctors who can handle both internal medicine and surgery, the veterinarians at this hospital do, and I am impressed by the high level of skill of each individual veterinarian. Although it's private practice because it's for animals, I don't feel the price is high, so I think it must be quite inexpensive.
I have great respect for them as a medical professional.

I've been a patient here since before they moved.

The head veterinarian always puts the animals first, and he genuinely cares about the pet owners. I'm so glad I met Dr. Yuchi. The consultation fees are also very reasonable. Even if the wait is two hours, or if I have to take a taxi from home, I can't imagine going anywhere other than Garden Animal Hospital.

I also feel at ease knowing that all the staff treat my pets with the same care and attention they would give their own.

The staff and doctors at this animal hospital are all very friendly and attentive. The director speaks English, which was a big plus for me as a foreigner. However, after a few visits, I felt that this clinic was not a good fit for my cat.
I brought my cat in because I was concerned about a possible bone problem. The director recommended that we get a CT scan. After the CT scan, my cat was so scared that he urinated all over the place.
Overall, I would not recommend this animal hospital to anyone with a cat. The staff may be friendly, but the director’s way of treating cats makes me worry about the safety of my pet.

LINE reservations were supposedly introduced for convenience? To reduce workload? But they still don't work at all, and the situation remains the same even when I show up to the hospital in person to make a reservation.

The LINE messages are full of things like "Come to the hospital immediately, if we're not in the hospital we'll skip your turn" and "warning messages (just to let you know)," so it seems like a system imposed on patients for self-preservation.

The hospital is also explaining LINE reservations and urging patients to make the necessary adjustments, but there's no benefit for the patients (if anything, it's a negative situation; as others have said, the wait times are long, and they were told via LINE to come earlier... they shouldn't have said that).

Just now, someone who had made a LINE reservation but had been kept waiting for a long time became angry and started yelling at them before leaving...

Excellent service
While there can be long waiting times, there are no excessive treatments, surgeries, or medications, and the doctors examine the animals with genuine care.
I am always grateful to the head veterinarian.
All of our family's pets have been cared for here, and they have always handled travel documents without any problems.
They also have a partner emergency hospital that is open at night, so subsequent treatment was always smooth.
If I had to mention one drawback, it would be that there may be differences in the doctors' abilities, so I recommend visiting several times to find a doctor that suits you.

I've been a patient here for almost 20 years now. Even though they've introduced online appointment booking via LINE, the wait times are still a bit long, but in return, they provide very thorough examinations. It was here that a tumor that another hospital had deemed nothing to worry about was actually discovered to be cancerous.

This is a veterinary clinic that primarily treats dogs and cats, but most visitors are dogs. Cats seem to be a minority, so it's probably best to avoid bringing a cat.

There's a "cat-priority area" in the waiting room, but it doesn't function properly when it's crowded. Dog owners sit there waiting without a care in the world. I had to ask the receptionist to move them.

Unlike individual clinics, there are multiple veterinarians, which is reassuring in case of an emergency.

I didn't request a specific veterinarian since it was my first visit, but you can request one if you wish.

The veterinarian I saw this time was kind and thorough, so I would like to use their services again, but...

Dogs can walk around freely, but cats are intimidated by the dogs' barking and have no choice but to wait in their carriers. I think cats feel uncomfortable in a veterinary clinic, so it would be appreciated if they could be a little more considerate.
When my dog ​​went to the hospital with cancer, they responded quickly and he is now doing well!!!

The other day, my dog ​​got a rabies vaccination. The director wasn't there, so I thought, "Anyone can give me a shot if it's just a shot," and asked a young doctor. He cried more in pain than ever before. He was traumatized after that and now hates going to the hospital. I was surprised that even a vaccination could make such a big difference. I should have asked the director after all.

2021: I live in Jiyugaoka. When my 7-month-old dog suffered from diarrhea for over a week, I went to three reputable veterinarians in the neighborhood, but none of them were very effective. A friend recommended this place, and as a last resort, I went here. They cured him right away with an accurate examination, testing, and diagnosis.

There are an increasing number of clean, stylish clinics, but I was often put off by the fact that they all have young doctors, rotate doctors, and perform treatments behind the scenes. However, this clinic handles an overwhelming number of cases, and the doctors appear to be very experienced.

Even though it's 30 minutes from my house and the wait time is two hours, this vet is well worth the trip.

Garden Animal Hospital is a wonderful animal hospital where we have been taking care of our four dogs for 15 years, ever since they were still located along Yamate-dori. We have twin 15-year-old miniature dachshunds and twin 8-year-old Kaninchen dachshunds. Dr. Yuchi and his staff have provided annual health checkups and other care, and have even saved our dogs' lives when they were seriously ill or injured. We are incredibly grateful for their care.

We were also introduced to Miyanse, a specialist in gray hair removal in Daikanyama, who has been taking care of our dogs and grooming them for the past 15 years.

I took my small dog to this animal hospital for a nail trim, but the service was far from professional. They cut the nails too short, causing most of them to bleed. I was extremely angry. I returned to the hospital and demanded an …

I've always trusted the head veterinarian. However, lately he seems to be too busy and is only reviewing test results instead of examining individual patients. The same goes for the staff. But I still think he's the most trustworthy veterinarian of all.
Although the level of response varies depending on the teacher, they will all be very attentive.

Dr. Yuchi took care of my beloved toy poodle for about 3-4 years. (He was so wonderful that I traveled all the way from Nagoya, where I live, to see him.)
He was a truly wonderful doctor, always treating me with love and care. …

I've been receiving their care for about 25 years. 
The staff works together to provide support to both the animals and the families. I trust everything about the director: his diagnosis and treatment, …

I went there for my first visit. I was prepared for a long wait, but I was guided in smoothly, and the doctor was kind and examined me thoroughly. I've been to many animal hospitals before, but I think this is the most accurate and reassuring hospital.
